newsitem.title: USA: TRW posts 12 percent profit rise, plans to cut 2,300 jobs.
newsitem.headline: TRW posts 12 percent profit rise, plans to cut 2,300 jobs.

text.p: TRW Inc., reporting a 12 percent increase in third-quarter profits, said Monday it was eliminating some 2,300 jobs worldwide as it streamlines manufacturing plants, primarily in its automotive businesses.

The diversified manufacturing company, which has about 66,500 employees, said its net income in the three months ended Sept. 30 rose to $105.2 million, or $1.61 a share, from $93.6 million, or $1.39 a share.

It added that, excluding special items and the results of the company's information services business, which it sold on Sept. 19, its earnings increased 10 percent to $86.2 million, or $1.31 a share, from $78.2 million, or $1.18 a share.

The company said the cash proceeds of $1.01 billion from the sale of the information services business, which accounted for about 5 percent of its revenues, will give it a stronger strategic position in the future.
TRW, whose automotive components business accounts for almost two-thirds of its revenue, said third-quarter sales grew by 3 percent to $2.32 billion from $2.25 billion.
The company said the special items included an after-tax gain of $242.4 million, or $3.67 a share, from the sale of the information services business.
Offsetting the gain was an after-tax charge of $233.4 million, or $3.53 a share, for restructuring its automotive and space and defence businesses.

"As a result of these actions, several manufacturing facilities located throughout the world will be closed or consolidated, and employment company-wide will be reduced by approximately 2,300," TWR said in a statement.

It said the charges related to reconfiguration of manufacturing plants, primarily in the automotive businesses, litigation and warranty expenses, contract and employee benefit reserves, and writedown of impaired assets.

"These actions will increase long-term value for our shareholders," Chairman Joseph T. Gorman said. "The cash component of these special charges is $101 million, and we expect to see a payback within the next three years."
For the first nine months of the year, TRW said its net income grew by 6 percent to $352.7 million, or $5.31 a share, from $331.4 million, or $4.97 a share.
Sales for the period expanded to $7.41 billion from $7.26 billion in the year-ago quarter.
TRW's stock slipped 12.5 cents to $93.50 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
